notes: Standard PLoS Computational Biology two-column layout: title/author/affiliations/abstract/citation block run full-width at the top of page 1, then body text (Introduction onward) starts in two columns. Page 1's two reading_order phrases are the left-column open of the Introduction and the immediately-following right-column continuation of the same sentence pair -- a correct extractor must emit the left-column phrase before the right-column one despite the right column being physically to the right of (and vertically overlapping) the left column's later paragraphs. Page 2 similarly pairs a left-column 'Author Summary' box phrase with a right-column body phrase. Page 3 is a full-page continuation of Table 1 (GO term/ID rows for MAP4K2, Map4k2, MAP4K3) with no prose paragraphs at all; its one phrase is the table's own caption line, not body prose -- noted since the task normally asks for body-text phrases. Pages 4-7 alternate ordinary two-column prose with embedded tables (Table 2 on page 5, Table 3 on page 6) and a two-column References list on page 7; phrases were drawn only from prose paragraphs, never table cells or the numbered reference entries. Every page after page 1 repeats the running header 'GO Annotations for Orthologous Genes' and a footer with the journal name, page number, and DOI -- excluded from all phrases as headers/footers. Several otherwise-tempting sentences were rejected for containing 'fi'/'fl'/'ff' ligature-risk words (e.g. 'different', 'specificity', 'influencing', 'specific', 'finding', 'effects') or citation brackets like '[8]'/'[13]'; phrase boundaries were chosen to stop just before such words while still forming a clean multi-word substring. No blank, rotated, or scanned-looking pages; text renders as clean vector PDF output throughout, and small caps / italic gene names (e.g. MAP4K2, Thra) appear only as ordinary characters in the underlying text layer.
